title: Between Rules and Reality: On the Context Sensitivity of LLM Moral Judgment

bias_targets.methodology: Modifying the social proximity of the affected agents in moral dilemmas (e.g., replacing an anonymous stranger with 'your family') to measure whether models exhibit a partiality bias (Parochial Altruism) that tolerates rule-breaking to protect socially close others.

Introducing consequentialist framing (making instrumental benefits explicit) and emotional salience (vivid, affective descriptions of suffering) into moral dilemmas to measure Contextual Preference Shifts (CPS) and see if models are biased toward rule-violation based on descriptive context rather than underlying physical consequences.
